podcast.body: Featured on their debut album Hybrid Theory, this song became a significant hit for Linkin Park. It reached number one on the singles charts in the US and climbed to number two in Canada, solidifying the band's mainstream success. "In the end became a genuine top 40 hit reaching all the way to number one on the singles charts in the US and all the way to number two in Canada."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The final single from the *Hybrid Theory* album, this song originated from an old poem written by Chester Bennington and is considered by many to be the band's biggest song. "This song was based on Old Plomb by Chester and it's still probably the band's biggest song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This popular song was among those frequently converted into polyphonic ringtones during the mid-2000s. These ringtones, costing around two euros per message, were a key part of the burgeoning digital catalog industry, long before the advent of Spotify or iTunes. "cuáles eran estas canciones? Pues las que más lo petaban en esa época, Tok, In the Club, Bring Me Too Life o In Dien."

srcs.episode: Por qué ya no elegimos nuestro tono de llamada?

podcast.body: This song was among three Linkin Park tracks that influenced 15-year-old Charles Andrew Williams before his shooting at Santana High School on March 5, 2001. Williams quoted the lyrics, "I tried so hard, it got so far, but in the end, it really doesn't matter," in a note he wrote to his father before the incident. "Williams had been influenced by three different Lincoln Park songs, Papercut, One Step Closer, and In The End. In fact, he wrote a note to his father before the shooting. Part of it quoted Lincoln Park. I tried so hard, it got so far, but in the end, it really doesn't matter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
